reader.requirement: A procedure-name of a declarative section (the section or any of its paragraphs) may be referenced from a different declarative section or from the nondeclarative portion only by PERFORM (including PERFORM THRU within the section); every other reference (GO TO, GO TO DEPENDING, ALTER ... TO PROCEED TO, SORT/MERGE INPUT or OUTPUT PROCEDURE) from outside that section must be refused, while references inside the same section stay legal.
reader.edition-search: Read CheckDeclarativesBoundary and ResolveProcedureOperand whole and grep them for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior: data.Edition appears only as the diagnostic sink (Error/Warning); the check is section identity plus the PERFORM/RESUME reference kind, the same at every edition (its own doc comment: 'Every edition').
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb362_declaratives_reference_boundary covers the legal PERFORM forms; GO TO DEPENDING, ALTER and SORT INPUT PROCEDURE into a declarative are not exercised at 85 by that witness

probes.printed: PERFORM D1-P, PERFORM D1, PERFORM D1-P THRU D1-Q from MAIN and PERFORM D1-Q from D2 all compile and run (D1 RAN CNT=1..3, D1-Q RAN, D2 PERFORMED D1-Q)
probes.expected: accepted: PERFORM is the one permitted reference

probes.printed: error COBOL2376: GO TO 'D1-P' ... in the nondeclarative portion
error COBOL2376: GO TO 'D1-Q' ... in a different declarative section, 'D2'
error COBOL2376: ALTER TO PROCEED TO 'D1-P'

reader.notes: Every statement's procedure-name operand passes ResolveProcedureOperand, which asks CheckDeclarativesBoundary of section identity and the PERFORM exemption, so all non-PERFORM verbs are refused by construction. Minor: at --std 85 the COBOL2376 message cites §2023:14.9.49.3 SR4 rather than the 1985 rule; the behaviour is right, the citation names another edition.
reader.at-2023: same checker, same diagnostics (no edition arm)
